findings.title: Identity read always flags a tracer bug on the traced replays
findings.claim: ident() compares the traced replay rows against the stored rows on every key that read_c1.key_class calls traffic (vv.py:209). run6.wrap (run6.py:83-86) gives 'E30|w1u500~trace' the values arm='w1u500~trace' and learner=None, while the stored row has 'w1u500' for both. 'arm' and 'learner' are not in read_c1.PROV (read_c1.py:594), so they count as traffic keys.
findings.failure: Simulated with the 18 stored rows plus traced copies carrying wrap's fields: traced.rule_diff = {nc~trace, lr400_16_1~trace: ['arm']} and learner_diff = {w1u500~trace: ['arm','learner']}, so tracer_bug=True (vv.py:223). remote_vv.sh:73 then says 'STOPPED: a traced replay differs from its stored row' after the smoke and replay, every time.
findings.fix: In the traced compare, skip the identity fields that carry the run's own name (arm, learner, cell_spec if needed), as c1.twin_diff does. Add a test that builds traced rows through run6.wrap.

findings.title: Smoke T0 always fails on the 600-m plain twins
findings.claim: at_length adds vv_obs at 600 m (vv.py:57-58), so the 600-m twins (vv.py:93-95) create a VV object, and VV.finish always writes vv_lanes (vv_merge.py:160). The 300-m twins have no vv flag and so no vv_lanes. t0_lengths pairs 'L600|X~untraced' with 'L300|X~untraced' and reports 'no 300-m twin' when the 300-m row lacks vv_lanes.
findings.failure: Replaying t0_lengths on the planned vv_smoke arms returns ['L600|w1u500~untraced 7493010: no 300-m twin', 'L600|nc~untraced 7493010: no 300-m twin']. smoke pass=False (vv.py:188), so remote_vv.sh:57 must() says STOPPED at the first step of the rental.
findings.fix: Run T0 only on the instrumented arms (skip names containing '~'), or give the 300-m twins vv_obs/vv_lanes too. Add a planted-row test of t0_lengths on plan('vv_smoke') arm names.

findings.title: A crash in the identity read is ignored and the run continues
findings.claim: 'read ident' runs through step(), not must(), and its exit code is discarded. The next two lines only test for action=stop and tracer_bug=True in ident.json.
findings.failure: If vv.py ident raises (malformed row, KeyError), ident.json is missing or stale from an earlier attempt. val prints nothing to the job log, both tests read empty and are false, and the script logs 'identity: ... disclosed = ' and starts the traces and the 8,640-run screen with no identity check (§3 build item 4).
findings.fix: Check the result positively: require val action == go and tracer_bug == False, or run ident through must() and remove any old ident.json before it runs.

findings.title: V1 reads CHECKS PASS with missing traced runs or twins
findings.claim: v1() skips the twin check silently when a twin row is absent (tw is None). It never checks that all 24+6 traced and twin rows are present. remote_vv.sh has a row-count check for vv_replay (line 70) but none for vv_trace.
findings.failure: A trace seed that crashes 3 times goes to drops.json, and V1 reports 'CHECKS PASS; visual check pending' on fewer runs. read_vv.py v1 on an empty rows file printed 'V1 CHECKS PASS; visual check pending' (tested).
findings.fix: In v1, require every planned ~trace/~untraced pair on both seeds (or pass the jobs file), and add a row-count check after 'stage vv_trace' like line 70.

findings.title: Smoke T3 replays overwrite the merge logs and never compare them
findings.claim: v5.with_measure rewrites only 'measure'. vv_log stays $R/vv_smoke/vv for both the a and b passes, and the file tag (vv_merge.py:170) is name__q__seed in both, so b overwrites a's merge and standing logs. vv_log_file is skipped (vv.py:161) and no gz comparison is made, although the docstring says rows and side files are equal.
findings.failure: Non-determinism in the merge log (order, positions) between two runs of the same config would not be detected. The stored smoke logs are those of the b pass.
findings.fix: Point vv_log to out/a/vv and out/b/vv as measure is, and compare the gz contents in T3.

findings.title: Smoke wall_s per arm mixes meter-on and meter-off runs
findings.claim: wall is keyed by name.split('~')[0], so 'L300|w1u500' averages the meter-on screen arm with its plain twin (no meter). §4 asks for 'measured seconds per run with the meter on'.
findings.failure: The printed wall time for L300 w1u500, lr400_16_1, p333 and nc understates the meter's overhead (each is the mean of one run with the meter and one without). The cost rate is unaffected, because remote_vv.sh:63 excludes '~' rows.
findings.fix: Key wall times by the full name, or exclude TWIN rows.

findings.title: vv_obs is never tested against a twin without it
findings.claim: Every 600-m arm, including the 'plain' twins, carries vv_obs (at_length, vv.py:58). So no twin pair can show that obs_check (which calls env._x_base(train=True), vv_merge.py:149) leaves the run unchanged. In practice it fills the same cache key the remap fills, so the risk is low.
findings.failure: If obs_check ever changed state (e.g. a future edit to _x_base), the twins would agree and the smoke would pass.
findings.fix: Leave vv_obs off the 600-m twins (keep x_remap), so the pair differs only in instruments.

findings.title: The smoke input check has no coverage assertion
findings.claim: x_out lists only rows with vv_c15_n and a nonzero vv_x_out. It does not require vv_x_acc_n > 0 for the 600-m learner rows, so the assertion passes trivially if no CAV is seen on 3a/4a or obs_check never runs.
findings.failure: A wiring slip that skipped obs_check would leave x_out empty and the smoke would pass.
findings.fix: Require vv_x_acc_n > 0 for every L600 learner row in the smoke.

findings.title: The reader's usage line lists options it does not have; the status line omits V3 bug lists
findings.claim: The docstring lists 'v1 ... [--replay ROWS]' and 'v3 ... [--workers N]', but argparse (lines 337-343) defines neither. remote_vv.sh passes the replay rows through --trace, which works. remote_vv.sh:84 prints the V2/V3 readings but not v3.json's bugs.meter/bugs.x_out or void.
findings.failure: A by-hand rerun with --replay fails with an argparse error. An x_out bug or a CPU void at 600 m is visible only inside v3.json, not in status.txt.
findings.fix: Fix the usage line, and add bugs and void to the final say line.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced with my own script (/tmp/claude-1000/-srv-shared-Workspace-phd-phd-speed-harmo-v5b1/2d269ac5-95be-4f04-801b-ec9cc9873355/scratchpad/vvcr/skeptic_runner/r12.py): the 18 stored rows plus traced copies passed through run6.wrap give action 'go', tracer_bug True. traced.rule_diff holds ['arm'] for nc~trace and lr400_16_1~trace on both seeds; learner_diff holds ['arm','learner'] for w1u500~trace. Cause as claimed: run6.wrap (docs/research/planb/run6.py:83-86) derives arm='w1u500~trace' and learner=None from the name, the stored rows carry 'w1u500'/'w1u500', and read_c1.key_class (read_c1.py:594-604) classes both keys as traffic, so vv.py:209 lists them and vv.py:223 sets tracer_bug. The rule arms alone trigger it on any CPU. vv.py ident then exits 1 (vv.py:257) and remote_vv.sh:73 stops after the smoke and replay, on every rental. No wrong reading, but the rental cannot get past the replay.

Add a planted test that builds the traced rows through run6.wrap.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced: vv.plan('vv_smoke') gives 24 arms; the two 600-m twins carry {accel_len, accel2_len, x_remap, vv_obs} and the four 300-m twins carry no vv flag (printed from the plan). vv_merge.wanted (vv_merge.py:24-25) is true for vv_obs alone, plant_sweep.py:385-386 then builds a VV, and VV.finish always writes vv_lanes (vv_merge.py:160). t0_lengths (vv.py:113-118) pairs 'L600|X~untraced' with 'L300|X~untraced', which has no vv_lanes. On planted rows it returns ['L600|w1u500~untraced 7493010: no 300-m twin', 'L600|nc~untraced 7493010: no 300-m twin'], so smoke pass is False (vv.py:188) and remote_vv.sh:57 (must) stops the rental after the smoke runs, every time.
verdicts.better_fix: One change fixes R2 and R7 together: take 'vv_obs' out of at_length (vv.py:58) and add it only in screen_arm and in the 600-m traced arms. The 600-m twins then build no VV, have no vv_lanes, and t0_lengths skips them at vv.py:113; the screen arms still pair L600|X with L300|X, both with vv_lanes. If vv_obs must stay on the twins, the alternative is to skip names containing '~' at vv.py:113. Add a planted-row test of t0_lengths on plan('vv_smoke') arm names.

verdicts.reason: The mechanism is as claimed: remote_vv.sh:71 uses step, not must, and lines 72-73 only test for the two bad values. I ran the script's val() on a missing file: stdout is empty, both tests are false, and the script would go on to the traces and the screen. I lower the severity because the gate fails open only if vv.py ident crashes, and I found no input that crashes it: it is pure Python, it ran clean on the stored rows plus wrap-built traced rows, rel_diff catches type and shape errors (read_c1.py:607-613), and line 70 already guarantees the row count. The stale-file case is not reachable in practice: a rerun with changed code is refused by pb.guard (pb.py:187-191, 'use a new folder'), and a rerun with the same code rewrites ident.json. If it did happen, 'end rc=1' is in status.txt and ident can be rerun on the fetched rows on the laptop, so the cost is at most one screen (my estimate from the reviewer's figures: under $2), not a wrong reading.
verdicts.better_fix: Two positive tests in place of lines 72-73: require action == go, else STOPPED; require tracer_bug == False, else STOPPED. No must() needed, and the specific stop messages stay. An 'rm -f ident.json' before line 71 is optional.

verdicts.reason: read_vv.py:314-316 skips the twin compare when the twin row is absent, and nothing counts the traced rows. I ran read_vv.py v1 on an empty rows file: it prints 'V1 CHECKS PASS; visual check pending' with rc 0. run6.execute returns normally with up to 3 crash-dropped seeds per arm (run6.py:136-145), and remote_vv.sh has a row-count test for vv_replay (line 70) but none after 'stage vv_trace' (line 76). The drops are written to status.txt (line 50), and V1 still needs the author's visual check, so minor stands.
verdicts.better_fix: The shell test alone suffices: after line 76, the same row-count test as line 70 for vv_trace. With all 24 rows present every ~trace row has its twin by construction of the plan. A check inside v1() would have to exempt the E30|...~trace replay rows, which have no twin by design (they are checked by ident).

verdicts.reason: v5.with_measure rewrites only 'measure' (docs/research/v505/v5.py:176-177). vv_log stays <smoke dir>/vv for passes a and b (vv.py:64, 157-158), and the file tag is name__q__seed in both (plant_sweep.py:458, vv_merge.py:170), so pass b overwrites pass a's log. T3 compares only the m_st_file arrays (vv.py:164-165); vv_log_file is in skip (vv.py:161) and is the same file name anyway. The exposure is small: the row-level counts taken from the same data (vv_merges, vv_merge_other, vv_merge_gone, vv_stand_n, vv_stand_s) are compared in T3, so only a difference in log contents with equal counts and equal traffic keys would be missed. The docstring's 'side files equal' is not true for the merge logs.
verdicts.better_fix: In smoke(), set vv_log to out/a/vv and out/b/vv next to with_measure, and compare the decompressed JSON of the two files (not the gz bytes: gzip writes a timestamp in its header, so byte equality would fail). About four lines. The lighter option is to correct the docstring and name the row-level counts as the T3 evidence for the logs.

verdicts.reason: vv.py:182 keys wall times by name.split('~')[0], so for L300 w1u500, lr400_16_1, p333 and nc the printed figure is the mean of one meter-on run and one plain twin (twins planned at vv.py:93-95). Section 4 of merge_vv.md asks for 'measured seconds per run with the meter on'. The other five L300 arms have no twin and print clean meter-on times, and the cost rate is unaffected (remote_vv.sh:63 drops '~' rows), so only the printed figure for four arms is diluted.
verdicts.better_fix: Key by r['name'] at vv.py:182 (one token); twins then print on their own lines and the meter's overhead per arm can be read directly.

verdicts.reason: The printed plan shows vv_obs on every 600-m arm, twins included, in vv_smoke; vv_trace builds its 600-m twins from the same at_length (vv.py:87-89). vv_obs is never on at 300 m. So no twin pair differs in vv_obs, and the twin check cannot show obs_check to be read-only, although section 3 asks for twin tests of each instrument. Risk is low today: obs_check (vv_merge.py:143-157) only calls getRoadID, reads env.xlast and calls env._x_base(train=True), which fills the cache key the remap already fills (b_env.py:893, 913-918; all nine arms have fix_x and x_remap). For no control the observation is not the CAV 4-tuple, so obs_check returns at once.
verdicts.better_fix: Same change as R2: keep x_remap in at_length, add vv_obs only to the screen arms and the 600-m traced arms. The twins then differ from their instrumented runs in every instrument, and R2's false T0 failure goes away with it.

verdicts.reason: vv.py:179 lists only rows that have vv_c15_n and a nonzero vv_x_out, and obs_checks (vv.py:135) skips rows without vv_c15_n. If obs_check never ran, or counted no vehicle on 3a/4a, the assertion passes on zero samples. I raise it from info to minor: the code has not yet run in a simulation, and this assertion is the only gate on the remapped inputs before 8,640 runs. The wiring looks right on reading (the CAV observation is a 4-tuple, b_env.py _obs return; obs_check is called after every step, plant_sweep.py:401-402), so I expect it to pass. The same gap exists for the meter: meter_bugs (vv.py:144) and read_vv.py derive (meter_ok, 'vv_m_step' not in r or ...) only test rows that contain vv_m_step, and VV.S is a defaultdict, so a meter that never counted passes the equality check while ttc_net is above 0.
verdicts.better_fix: In smoke(): require vv_x_acc_n > 0 for every L600 learner row, and treat a 300-m screen row with ttc_net > 0 and no vv_m_step as a meter bug (also in read_vv.py's meter_ok). Two short conditions.

verdicts.reason: The usage text at read_vv.py:3-4 lists --replay and --workers; argparse (read_vv.py:337-343) defines neither, and remote_vv.sh:77 passes the replay rows through --trace, which works. remote_vv.sh:84 prints the V2 outcome and the V3a/V3b readings only.
